title: EAC Scholarship Programme (EACSP) Phase II: KfW-funded two-year master's in another EAC country (IUCEA, cohort 4)
organization: Inter-University Council for East Africa (IUCEA), for the East African Community and the Federal Republic of Germany (KfW funding)
overview: A regional programme that funds two-year master's degrees at partner universities in Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania and Uganda for nationals of the eight EAC partner states, the Democratic Republic of the Congo included. The cohort 4 call (20 August to 10 September 2026) lists business-related master's such as an MBA, logistics and supply chain management, human resource management, taxation (INES-Ruhengeri in Rwanda) and innovation and entrepreneurship management. The cohort 4 window is closed; this record is here to watch for the next cohort.
program_dates: Two-year master's; students 'may commence their studies at the earliest available intake' of the host university. Scholarship offers were due to be communicated in December 2026.
deadline_text: Cohort 4: 'Opening date: 20th August 2026. Closing date: 10th September 2026, not later than 17:00 hours, East African Time.' Closed. No later cohort call has been found.
deadline_timezone: East Africa Time (EAT, UTC+3), per the call
expected_next_cycle: The call says Phase II 'commenced in October 2025 and is expected to support at least 280 students across three cohorts'. Cohort 4 closed on 10 September 2026 and results were due in December 2026; a later cohort has not been announced on the pages read.
funding_details: One return economy-class air ticket between the scholar's home country and the host country, at the start and at the end of studies
Full tuition fees paid directly to the host university
EUR 200 arrival allowance; monthly stipend of EUR 380 'to cover accommodation, meals, local transport and other living expenses'
EUR 650 lump sum for study materials; one-time EUR 1,500 study and research allowance
Medical insurance for the duration of the scholarship; visa or entry fee 'where payment of entry pass into the host country or student pass is required'
The call does not use the words 'fully funded'; up to 120 scholarships in cohort 4
participation_fee: No scholarship application fee stated; the host university's own application fee must be paid 'where applicable'
stipend: EUR 380 a month plus EUR 200 on arrival, EUR 650 study materials and a one-time EUR 1,500 study and research allowance
eligibility: Citizen of one of the 8 EAC Partner States (Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kenya, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, United Republic of Tanzania, Uganda)
Below 35 years of age at the time of application
Applies to study in an EAC Partner State other than the country of citizenship
A Bachelor's degree with a minimum of Second Class Upper Division, Distinction or equivalent
Has applied for admission to an eligible master's programme at a partner university
Complete scholarship application (online form plus a zipped set of PDF documents emailed to IUCEA) within the application period
The programme targets 'academically talented but financially disadvantaged students'; applications are in English
nationality_requirements: Citizens of the 8 EAC Partner States, which include the Democratic Republic of the Congo, studying outside their own country
age_requirement: Below 35 at the time of application
education_requirement: Bachelor's degree with at least Second Class Upper Division, Distinction or equivalent; qualifications obtained outside the host country must be equated by the host country's higher education authority before admission
language_requirement: Applications in English; an English proficiency certificate (IELTS, TOEFL) is an optional document 'where applicable'
other_requirements: Two stages: apply for admission to the partner university, and separately apply for the scholarship (admission alone is not an application)
Mandatory documents include ID or passport, photo, proof of university admission application, certified bachelor's certificate and transcript, CV, academic and professional reference letters
Optional documents used to assess financial need include bank statements, payslips and evidence of dependents
documents_required: Certified bachelor's degree certificate and transcript
application_process: Part A: apply for admission to an eligible master's programme in an EAC country other than your own, saying you intend to apply for the EAC scholarship
Part B: complete the online scholarship form and email one zipped folder of PDF documents named by document code to eacsp@iucea.org and scholarships@adroitconsultinternational.com
Each programme applied for needs its own form and its own email

sources.label: IUCEA call for applications, cohort 4 (PDF hosted by the University of Dar es Salaam, a partner institution)

eligibility_reason: DRC nationality, age under 35 and the 2024 bachelor's degree fit. The profile does not record the degree grade (Second Class Upper Division or equivalent is required), financial need, or admission to a partner programme, and the DRC degree must be equated by the host country's authority.
potential_issues: The cohort 4 window closed on 10 September 2026; no later cohort has been announced
The official IUCEA site did not answer (connection reset) and the UNHCR Rwanda copy of the detailed call returned 403, so the call was read on a partner university's copy only
The call does not say 'fully funded'; the stipend of EUR 380 a month has to cover accommodation, meals and local transport
A degree grade of Second Class Upper Division or equivalent is required and is not recorded; DRC grading must be converted by the host country's authority
Admission to the partner programme must be sought separately and the university's own fee paid
benefits: Leadership development, mentoring and networking among future regional leaders
Participation in at least one extracurricular event
relevance_reason: Names the DRC as eligible, takes applicants under 35 and includes an MBA, logistics and supply chain, human resource management, taxation and innovation and entrepreneurship master's, which suit a business administration degree. Closed for now, so the value is in preparing for the next cohort.

visa.required: Yes, for study in another EAC state (not read on a visa page)
visa.support: Visa or entry fee covered 'where payment of entry pass into the host country or student pass is required'

upfront_cost_risk: Low: no scholarship application fee; host university application fee may apply
action: Cohort 4 is closed. Ask eacsp@iucea.org whether a further cohort is planned and when it opens. Meanwhile check your Licence result against the Second Class Upper Division rule and shortlist business programmes such as the MBA or the supply chain master's at the partner universities in Kenya, Rwanda and Tanzania.
notes: Found through a web search on 2 November 2026 (several aggregators repeat it); the call PDF was read on the University of Dar es Salaam site. Business-related programmes in the cohort 4 table: KCA University (MBA; MSc Human Resource Management; MSc Development Finance), Kibabii University (MSc Logistics and Supply Chain Management), USIU-Africa (MSc Organisational Development and Management; MA Business Microfinance), INES-Ruhengeri, Rwanda (MSc Taxation), NM-AIST Tanzania (MSc Innovation and Entrepreneurship Management), Daystar University (MSc Economics).
